question: What chemical property of raltegravir and related drugs explains its ability to inhibit the HIV virus integrase ?:

options.opa: They are basic compounds, which once protonated block an ion channel associated with the enzyme.
options.opb: They are alkylating agents, capable of covalently binding to a cysteine ​​residue of the active site of the enzyme.
options.opc: They are chelating agents, capable of coordinating two Mg2 + cations of the active site of the enzyme.
options.opd: They are analogues of the transition state of the hydrolysis reaction catalyzed by the enzyme.
